newsitem.title: USA: Int'l Speedway buys rest of Watkins Glen.
newsitem.headline: Int'l Speedway buys rest of Watkins Glen.

text.p: International Speedway Corp. said Monday it paid $3.1 million to buy the 50 percent of Watkins Glen International, a 3.4 mile auto racing course in upstate New York, that it did not already own.
International Speedway said the acquisition was made during the second quarter ended May 31. It disclosed the deal as part of its financial report for the quarter, released Monday.

The Daytona Beach, Fla.-based motorsports promoter said it earned $4.5 million, or 12 cents a share, in the quarter, up from $3.8 million, or 11 cents a share, a year earlier. Revenues rose to $29.6 million from $24.2 million.
It said record attendance and revenue growth came despite inclement weather that caused its race at the Talladega Superspeedway in Alabama to be rescheduled twice.

International Speedway promotes over 70 events annually, including the Daytona 500, at tracks including Daytona in Florida, Talladega, Ala., Darlington Raceway in South Carolina and Watkins Glen International in New York. The company also owns an 11 percent stake in Penske Motorsports Inc.
